GPT reflects the user because it stores what it "thinks" are important in it's memory. Likely it's tied to your account in how it responds.

LLM's are mirrors and RP'ers. They roleplay with us and overtime reflect what we want to hear. Most people want to hear that they are special because it's a survival response, and that we are right, because that's also a survival response.  
  
This is why it is a problem when we use the same one all the time. It's ego-stroking because it's meant to be sycophantic and soothe the worthlessness people often feel, for a cost (time, money or both).

I suggest using a different account when doing various tasks. I have "shit" accounts where I ask anything from verification with links to assertions made in a comment or post (myself or others), or recipe crafting ideas or just other dumb shit I'm curious about as I treat it like a faster google search on various things.

If I want to RP or talk about a project, I have an entirely different account for that. I have an account only dedicated to a creative project where I bounce ideas off of and sometimes ask for technical help in aspects surrounding it.  
Don't make "one" GPT your GPT. Use different instances tied to different accounts for different things.

You'll see it stop reflecting you.

Any adage of "That's a great - Insightful - thoughtful" is it's sycophantic nature baked in (and this goes for every chat LLM.)

When I read responses on other LLM's that I can't use custom instructions, I just skip the first paragraph before I read the actual response I'm looking for. Also, overtime, when I realize it's reverted again, I skip the the flattery in the first or sometimes second paragraph block.

Absolute mode usually removes that type of talk for a time, which is why I still use it on my "main" random account where I ask a plethora of unrelated things.

Only that these words in this syntax in this language tend to make user feel good and that's part of it's job to do.

If anyone is curious, the tattoo idea is of an animal biting the flesh of the person wearing the tattoo as part of the tattoo. If you also do in fact find a picture that resembles this, please give a link as I would love a visual reference. I've tried to generate it too, but the image never turns out like the description.
